subject: Nexus Alliance: architecture gate & acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@nexus-consulting.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Iyengar <asha.iyengar@nexus-consulting.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nexus x Redwood — kickoff & technical gate

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for taking the intro call last week. Nexus is excited to move toward a formal technical gate so our engineering teams can run a brief compatibility pass and scope an integration pilot.

High-level ask: can Redwood share a small reference architecture and an acceptance checklist (SLOs, auth flows, dataplane requirements) so Nexus can validate the connector approach against our managed offering? In return we can deliver an initial POC plan and a filled security questionnaire within two weeks.

Proposed next step: 30–45 minute technical kickoff this week. Who from your side would you like on the call?

Attaching a short Nexus one-pager for context.

Best,
Raj
Principal Architect | Nexus Consulting
[Attachment: nexus-onepager.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@nexus-consulting.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexus x Redwood — kickoff & technical gate

Raj — thanks for the note and the one-pager. Happy to run a technical gate.

We're available for a kickoff on Wednesday 08/11 at 10:00am PT or Thursday 08/12 at 11:00am PT. Please pick whichever works. For the call I'll include Marissa (solution architect) and Sergio (partner integrations lead) — they'll drive the architecture and acceptance criteria.

Quick context on what we'll share prior to the call:
- A concise reference architecture doc (deployment flavors: hosted API, dedicated pool, private VPC)
- A short acceptance checklist (routing, auth, data retention, latency targets)
- A sample webhook/auth flow and recommended retry/backoff guidance

I've attached the reference architecture draft and a template acceptance checklist — these are intentionally terse so we can iterate during the call.

Attachments: "redwood-reference-arch-v1.docx", "acceptance-checklist-template.xlsx"

Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Nexus gate prep checklist

Quick internal note before the kickoff:

1) Security items to have ready (ask Nexus to send):
   - Completed Nexus security questionnaire (we should pre-seed with SOC 2 controls they use)
   - Any data residency constraints for pilot data sets

2) Technical validation scope (we should confirm on call):
   - Auth: API key vs mTLS; must confirm if Nexus requires mutual TLS for their connector
   - Throughput: expected peak qps for the POC (we need sample traffic pattern)
   - Model selection: Nexus said they plan to test generation + embeddings; verify model families and sequence lengths
   - Failure/fallback behavior: define acceptable degraded-mode behavior (model downgrade or cached response)

3) Deliverables for a go/no-go decision after POC:
   - Successful end-to-end request flow in the target deployment (hosted or VPC)
   - Latency within agreed SLO (p50/p95 targets agreed)
   - Passing security review items

I'll draft a short runbook fragment during the call. Sergio — can you own the acceptance criteria writeup and the final doc we send to Nexus?

-Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@nexus-consulting.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Nexus technical gate — acceptance criteria & next steps

Raj / Asha — thanks for the call today. Good alignment across teams. Below is a concise acceptance checklist and next steps — please review and confirm.

Acceptance Criteria (post-POC):
- End-to-end request completed in targeted deployment (Hosted API or Private VPC) with authentication flow documented and reproducible.
- Average latency p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 650ms for Nexus test corpus (50–512 tokens).
- Model fallback policy implemented for outages (automatic fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant).
- Data retention and logging configuration documented; no customer data persisted beyond retention window unless explicitly requested.
- Security questionnaire completed and redwood security team has no open critical findings.

Deliverables by Nexus within 10 business days:
- Filled security questionnaire (see attached spreadsheet)
- Sample traffic profile (QPS, payload distribution)
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., vendor-managed keys / KMS requirements)

Attachments: "nexus-technical-answers.xlsx"
Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cNexusSolution (shared design folder), HS-12345 (HubSpot record)

Next steps:
1) Nexus provides the questionnaire + sample traffic by 08/23.
2) Redwood will run a short POC (2–3 days of test traffic) in a sandbox environment; results + metrics will be shared.
3) Post-POC review and decision on pilot expansion.

If that matches Nexus' expectations, we'll issue a short SOW draft for the pilot and timeline.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Partner Integrations Lead | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0110
